key_big: Light comes in photons of energy E = hf.
key_sub: Moving clocks run slow: Δt = γΔt₀.
body_html:
How to think about it

A photon has energy E = hf = hc/λ (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s). In the photoelectric effect, a photon frees an electron only if hf is at least the work function: Ek,max = hf − W. Particles also behave as waves with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.

Special relativity: the laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame and light travels at c for every observer. So moving clocks run slow (Δt = γΔt₀), moving lengths contract (L = L₀/γ), with γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²), and mass is a form of energy (E = mc²). The standard model builds matter from quarks and leptons, with forces carried by bosons.

Example

Energy of a photon of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz?

E = hf = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 5.0 × 10¹⁴

Answer: 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

Example

γ for v = 0.6c?

γ = 1 ÷ √(1 − 0.36)

Answer: 1.25

Common mistakes

  • Thinking brighter light gives photoelectrons more energy: it gives more electrons; frequency sets the energy.
  • Applying time dilation to the clock that is at rest with the observer.
  • Saying a proton is a fundamental particle: it is made of quarks.

faq.q: Why does the photoelectric effect support the photon model?
faq.a: Below a threshold frequency no electrons are emitted however bright the light, which waves cannot explain.

faq.q: What is a muon's lifetime evidence for?
faq.a: Muons made high in the atmosphere reach the ground because their clocks run slow at high speed (time dilation).

items.q: Light of wavelength 210 nm falls on copper (work function 4.7 eV). Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons in eV.
items.e: Photon energy = hc/λ = 5.92 eV. Ek(max) = hf − φ = 5.92 − 4.7 = 1.22 eV.

items.q: Light of wavelength 220 nm falls on copper (work function 4.7 eV). Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons in eV.
items.e: Photon energy = hc/λ = 5.65 eV. Ek(max) = hf − φ = 5.65 − 4.7 = 0.951 eV.

items.q: Light of wavelength 180 nm falls on silver (work function 4.3 eV). What stopping potential is needed to stop the fastest photoelectrons?
items.e: eVs = hf − φ, so Vs = 6.91 − 4.3 = 2.61 V.

items.q: Observers on Earth measure the journey on a spacecraft moving at 0.5c as 23.1 years. What is the proper time measured on board?
items.e: Proper time t₀ = t ÷ γ = 23.1 ÷ 1.15 = 20 years.

items.q: A muon (lifetime 2.2 µs in its own frame) moves at 0.99c. Taking time dilation into account, how far does it travel, as measured from Earth, in one lifetime?
items.e: Earth time = γt₀ = 7.09 × 2.2 µs; d = v × γt₀ = 4.63e+03 m. This is why muons from the upper atmosphere reach the ground.

items.q: A spacecraft moves at 0.6c relative to Earth. On board, the journey lasts 2 years. How long does it last as measured from Earth?
items.e: Moving clocks run slow: t = γt₀ = 1.25 × 2 = 2.5 years.
